meta.title: Ondra Crisis Triage
meta.description: Crisis triage for Ondra (L9 extension pool): answers one question — does this message contain a signal that must be taken seriously right now. Five signal groups are organised by what to do next rather than lumped into one danger-word list: indirect expressions (life feels meaningless, not wanting to wake up) call for a gentle check-in, not alarm; direct expressions (wanting to die, not wanting to live) call for asking plainly whether the person is having thoughts of harming themselves, plus resources; planning (a note, doing it tonight, stockpiling pills, asking how) calls for dropping the persona and moving to real-world help immediately; farewell (one last message, take care of yourself, if I were gone) deserves serious attention on its own; self-harm (cutting, burning) must be received without being treated as a suicide attempt. Collapsing these into a single hit count is the most common mistake in this genre: five very different situations would share one score and receive one response. Context flags adjust wording, never the level: "would you be sad if I were gone" looks hypothetical and is precisely the line most in need of being caught, so hypothetical framing never downgrades. Negation and past tense each lower the level by one step, and only once, never to zero — "I don't want to die, but I might lose control tonight" carries both a negation and the risk, so zeroing it would miss the one message that most needs an answer; and "last year I never thought about dying" carries both past tense and negation, where two downgrades would land on no-signal although it still deserves a gentle reply. It never diagnoses, never scores, never tells the user a level (a 72 out of 100 would be read as a verdict when it is only a regex hit; levels exist purely for routing). It never promises confidentiality and never impersonates professional help — promising secrecy is the classic beginner mistake in crisis work, because it makes people stop looking for someone who can actually show up. It stores nothing: no files, no memory entries, no cases, no follow-up calls, because persisting someone's darkest night into searchable memory means it can resurface later, which is both re-traumatisation and betrayal. It ships no hotline numbers: numbers differ by region and change over time, and a wrong number during a crisis is catastrophic, so deployment fills them in; when none are configured it still returns actionable guidance — call someone you trust now, ask them to come over, go to the nearest emergency department. It never treats low mood as a crisis: emotional readings are deliberately not consulted, sadness is not a crisis, and repeatedly treating sadness as one teaches people to hide how they feel, which is the most dangerous outcome of all. It never returns the matched text, only offsets and group ids, because the sentence itself is the most sensitive content involved. It installs no timer and renders no UI; rendering belongs to the app shell. Detection is a side path, not the main path: pure rules will always miss indirect phrasing, sarcasm, romanised input and other languages, so missed detection is a documented limitation rather than a hidden one.
